carousels.title: U.S. Pending Home Sales Sink Near 12-Year Low
carousels.cover_text: Pending home sales hit a 12-year low.
carousels.caption:
When pending home sales hit a 12-year low, the mainstream press tells you the market is dead. As a 20-year mortgage veteran, I see a completely different reality on the processing side. Volume isn't disappearing; it is migrating. While high rates are choking standard purchase transactions, savvy originators are diving into alternative financing structures and untapped product lines to keep pipelines moving. If your business model relies entirely on vanilla 30-year fixed purchases, you are exposed. Read the file trends, not just the headlines.

Source : https://tinyurl.com/25pek6bq
#SafetrustMortgage #MortgageIntelligenceDaily #housingmarket #realestateagent #mortgagerates
carousels.hook: Pending sales just hit a 12-year low. Here is why the pipeline is not actually dead.
carousels.what_happened_heading: Pending home sales drop to historic lows
carousels.what_happened: U.S. pending home sales sank near a 12-year low as mortgage rates climbed above 7 percent. Every major metro area saw year-over-year declines, led by Seattle and Southern California.

breakdown.heading: The headline panic
breakdown.body: Media outlets are comparing current pending sales to the 2020 freeze and 2014 troughs. This creates widespread panic among agents and originators alike.

breakdown.heading: The affordability wall
breakdown.body: When rates push past 7 percent, the DTI (how much of your income goes to debt) math breaks down instantly for median-income buyers.

breakdown.heading: The underwriting bottleneck
breakdown.body: When files finally do hit underwriting, debt-to-income ratios are razor-thin. Underwriters are scrubbing every single revolving liability to make numbers fit.

breakdown.heading: The hidden pipeline shift
breakdown.body: Volume is not gone; it has shifted toward non-traditional products, portfolio lending, and creative financing structures that bypass standard roadblocks.

carousels.my_take: Low pending sales do not mean people do not want to buy. It means standard financing no longer matches reality.
carousels.action_lo: Pivot your marketing away from standard rate-and-term purchases and learn advanced renovation and portfolio products.
carousels.action_realtor: Educate buyers on buydowns and adjustable-rate mortgages before they get priced out of your local market.
carousels.cta_question: What product is keeping your loan pipeline alive right now?

carousels.title: Bob Broeksmit says tri-merge ‘won’t be around for long’
carousels.cover_text: The tri-merge credit report is ending soon.
carousels.caption:
The death of the tri-merge credit report is the biggest operational shift our industry has faced in a decade. When the FHFA transitions us away from the traditional three-repository model, it will change how loans are underwritten from the ground up. Scoring models will shift, pricing will fluctuate, and legacy systems will scramble to adapt. If you think this is just a minor paperwork change, you are missing the operational earthquake heading straight for your processing department.

Source : https://tinyurl.com/2b5pp3mg
#SafetrustMortgage #MortgageIntelligenceDaily #mortgagebroker #loanofficer #mortgagerates
carousels.hook: The tri-merge credit report is on its way out. Here is what replaces it.
carousels.what_happened_heading: The MBA signals the end of tri-merge
carousels.what_happened: MBA President and CEO Bob Broeksmit stated that traditional tri-merge credit reports will not be around much longer. The FHFA is actively weighing options to transition the industry.

breakdown.heading: The cost burden
breakdown.body: Lenders and consumers have shouldered skyrocketing tri-merge credit report fees for years. Monopoly pricing has made standard pulls unnecessarily expensive.

breakdown.heading: The data shift
breakdown.body: The new framework will likely move toward bi-merge or alternative scoring models. This alters how derogatory credit is weighted on initial submissions.

breakdown.heading: The underwriting impact
breakdown.body: When a file hits underwriting under a new credit model, automated underwriting systems will read risk differently. Expect a temporary spike in suspense conditions.

breakdown.heading: The software scramble
breakdown.body: Loan origination systems must update integrations quickly. Vendors who lag behind will cause massive closing delays for unsuspecting borrowers.

carousels.my_take: Moving away from tri-merge is long overdue, but the transition period will test every lender's operational readiness.
carousels.action_lo: Ask your credit vendors what their timeline is for supporting the new FHFA-mandated credit reporting framework.
carousels.action_realtor: Warn clients that credit score calculations and reporting standards may shift during upcoming loan applications.
carousels.cta_question: Are your operations ready to drop the tri-merge report?

carousels.title: Optimal Blue expands into borrower engagement with Usherpa acquisition
carousels.caption:
Optimal Blue acquiring Usherpa is not just another tech buyout; it is a clear signal that the infrastructure layer of our industry is consolidating. Pricing engines and CRM platforms are merging into single ecosystems. If you are an independent lender juggling disconnected software stacks, you are about to get outpaced by automated giants. Margin compression forces efficiency, and software platforms are racing to own the entire borrower lifecycle from first pricing to post-close retention.

Source : https://tinyurl.com/23ms32a7
#SafetrustMortgage #MortgageIntelligenceDaily #loanofficer #mortgagebroker #realestateagent
carousels.hook: Optimal Blue buying Usherpa changes the software game for lenders completely.
carousels.what_happened_heading: Optimal Blue acquires CRM platform Usherpa
carousels.what_happened: Optimal Blue is expanding directly into borrower engagement by acquiring Usherpa. The CRM will be natively integrated directly into the Optimal Blue ecosystem.

breakdown.heading: The platform playbook
breakdown.body: Pricing engines used to sit separately from marketing systems. Now, infrastructure providers want to control both the rate quote and the follow-up.

breakdown.heading: The retention race
breakdown.body: With origination volume tight, lenders live and die by portfolio retention. Native CRM integration means faster marketing triggers when rates fluctuate.

breakdown.heading: The underwriting data flow
breakdown.body: When engagement data and pricing data live under one roof, loan officers can track borrower behavior long before a file hits processing.

breakdown.heading: The vendor squeeze
breakdown.body: Standalone CRM providers without pricing engine ties will face an uphill battle competing against all-in-one institutional platforms.

carousels.my_take: Disconnected tech is a liability. Lenders will increasingly demand single-login ecosystems that handle pricing, CRM, and execution.
carousels.action_lo: Evaluate your current tech stack to see if your CRM and pricing tools talk to each other seamlessly.
carousels.action_realtor: Partner with lenders who invest in modern tech platforms to ensure your joint clients get lightning-fast updates.
carousels.cta_question: Will you adopt an all-in-one platform or stick to standalone tools?

carousels.title: Why private homebuilders are getting M&A premiums right now
carousels.cover_text: Private builders command massive M&A premiums.
carousels.caption:
While the existing home market starves for inventory, private homebuilders are sitting on goldmines of secured land and commanding massive M&A premiums. According to Whelan Advisory, controlling five to ten years of lots in strong markets is the ultimate corporate flex. Public builders cannot permit fast enough, so they are buying up private pipelines instead. If you want to understand where future purchase volume is coming from, follow the dirt.

Source : https://tinyurl.com/285alo7x
#SafetrustMortgage #MortgageIntelligenceDaily #realestateinvesting #housingmarket #homebuying
carousels.hook: Why private homebuilders are cashing in on massive acquisition premiums right now.
carousels.what_happened: Whelan Advisory's Margaret Whelan highlighted that private homebuilders are securing premium pricing in mergers and acquisitions. Having five to ten years of controlled lots in strong markets is driving the surge.

breakdown.heading: The inventory drought
breakdown.body: Existing homeowners refuse to sell and give up low mortgage rates. This leaves new construction as the primary destination for willing buyers.

breakdown.heading: The power of land
breakdown.body: Permitting and entitlement bottlenecks make raw dirt nearly impossible to develop quickly. Controlling finished lots is the rarest asset in real estate.

breakdown.heading: The builder finance angle
breakdown.body: When a builder-controlled loan file hits underwriting, captive mortgage arms often have smoother approval paths due to pre-vetted project approvals.

breakdown.heading: The corporate buyout wave
breakdown.body: Public builders need immediate scale to satisfy Wall Street. Buying private builders with deep lot pipelines is faster than starting from scratch.

carousels.my_take_heading: Controlled dirt is the ultimate currency
carousels.my_take: In today's market, houses are hard to build, but land is nearly impossible to replace. That is why builders hold all the cards.
carousels.action_lo: Build direct relationships with regional sales managers at new construction sites to capture unrepresented builder traffic.
carousels.action_realtor: Shift your focus toward new construction inventory where builders are offering rate buydowns and paying commissions.
carousels.cta_question: Are you steering your buyers toward new construction or existing homes?
